results.controlIntent: a. Use internal system clocks to generate time stamps for audit records; and b. Record those time stamps for audit records such that the time stamps meet [Assignment: organization-defined granularity of time measurement] and satisfy one or more of the following: use Coordinated Universal Time; have a fixed local time offset from Coordinated Universal Time; include the local time offset as part of the time stamp.

judgment.rationale: Both retrieved CloudTrail events for the churn-predictor-endpoint contain ISO 8601 timestamps with the "Z" (UTC) suffix, confirming: (a) timestamps are generated by AWS's internal system clock, and (b) timestamps are recorded in Coordinated Universal Time at second-level granularity. The CreateEndpoint event (ad7ee93f) records "2025-12-01T11:00:00Z" and the UpdateEndpoint event (2ab52b4b) records "2026-03-15T14:22:00Z". Both satisfy the UTC requirement of AU-8.r0(b). The configuration is substantively adequate — AWS CloudTrail natively uses internal system clocks and UTC for all audit records. Confidence is medium rather than high because the organization's specific defined granularity requirement (e.g., millisecond precision) was not available for comparison; if the organization requires sub-second granularity, the current second-level timestamps may fall short.
gaps: Organization-defined granularity requirement (e.g., millisecond vs. second) not available — cannot confirm timestamps meet the specific threshold defined by the organization.
No evidence of explicit NTP/time-sync configuration for the underlying compute infrastructure to confirm internal system clock accuracy.
No policy document retrieved specifying the organization's time-stamp standard for audit records.
